overview: This House resolution formally expresses the House of Representatives' deep sorrow at the death of Lindsey Graham, a U.S. Senator from South Carolina. It directs the Clerk of the House to send the resolution to the Senate and a copy to his family. It also provides that the House adjourn for the day as a further sign of respect for his memory. It is a customary memorial resolution and does not change any law. The House adopted it on July 13, 2026.
for: Supporters say it is a long-standing and appropriate tradition for the House to formally honor a sitting member of Congress who has died and offer condolences to the family.
against: Critics say it is a symbolic gesture that does not change any law or spending, though resolutions like this are rarely disputed.
